figmaExecutionNotes: Use a full-page dark theme across all sections; keep section background transitions intentional rather than alternating randomly.
Hero must be fully visible and scrollable into the rest of the page; do not stop the page at the hero.
Center the trust logic around logos/badges, since trust logos are the dominant proof strategy.
Do not use grid inside grid for the feature sections; prefer stacked cards or simple multi-column cards only where readability remains high.
Use a professional human-facing hero treatment if a human face media asset exists; keep any hero media authentic and avoid generated visuals layered on top.
If hero media is MP4, represent it as MP4 in Figma framing; do not convert it into a still image.
Include the creative gallery section with video and other media as a distinct section between the two product feature blocks.
Do not add unsupported sections such as pricing, testimonials, news, or a form because the input does not provide content for them.
Maintain implementation-friendly spacing and section naming for direct Figma handoff and component reuse.

heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro deliver premium image generation, audio-video synthesis, and enterprise-ready creative control for teams that need speed, fidelity, and consistency.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use an unexpected hero built like a premium creative command center: full-width dark mesh-gradient background with subtle grid lines and warm bronze glow, then place the copy in a left weighted content block while the media becomes a layered right-side dashboard stack. The visual stack should combine one large product/result preview, one smaller video-generation tile, and one thin control-strip mockup to communicate both Seedream and Seedance at once. Make the CTA buttons solid bronze, with a strong primary action and a secondary ghost action. Add floating parameter chips and a faint noise texture for depth. Avoid lifestyle imagery and human faces; keep everything product-centric, cinematic, and interface-led. The first trust band should sit directly beneath the hero with logo-led proof, and at least one adjacent section should switch to light background for contrast while the next feature block returns to dark.

repetitionBreakers: Hero uses a split studio-media composition; the next section shifts to a tight 3-step process on a darker band.
Proof appears as a logo grid immediately after the process, then product sections switch into alternating visual-first panels.
Image and video product blocks use different interaction patterns so adjacent sections never repeat the same visual rhythm.
Testimonials are compressed into a high-trust carousel/grid before the final CTA to re-energize the page.
Final conversion section becomes a contained floating card to close with a different density and background from the product story.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro by ByteDance | AI Image & Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Create high-quality AI images and videos with ByteDance’s Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Explore a 3-step workflow, recognisable proof logos, premium features, and a single Get started CTA.

sections.backgroundTreatment: dark studio gradient with subtle panel overlays, bronze accent glow, and interface-edge framing
sections.designNote: Hero must answer what this is, who it is for, and what to do next in one glance. Keep the copy content-first and continuity-driven: headline should clearly state AI image and video generation, subheadline should call out creative teams and enterprise buyers, and the only CTA button should read 'Get started'. Use a right-side media stack with product UI frames, a video tile, and generation result previews to make the output feel tangible above the fold.

sections.backgroundTreatment: compact dark strip with numbered steps and a thin bronze divider line
sections.designNote: Insert the warm-traffic 3-step sequence here, kept under 60 seconds: 1) add prompt, image, or script, 2) refine output with model controls, 3) export high-quality image or video. Use a concise dashboard-like step rail with one short line per step. This section should feel fast, operational, and low-friction. Avoid repeating the hero layout; make it narrower and more utility-led.

Use recognisable customer-style logos as the dominant proof signal. Since brand logos are available as a proof type, show a clean 3-6 logo row/grid rather than metrics. Keep it restrained, centered, and high-contrast on the dark band. If logo assets are limited at implementation time, replace with a clean metric strip, but the blueprint should prefer logos-first because trust is warm and early.

Use two distinct product blocks with alternating visual emphasis. First block: Seedream 4.5 in a spotlight-plus-preview treatment, highlighting text-image alignment, 1K-4K output, typographic rendering, identity-preserving multi-image composition, and structural fidelity. Second block: Seedance 1.5 Pro in a split-panel narrative with a strong preview tile for video output and a compact feature list emphasizing text-to-video, audio-visual sync, multilingual lip-sync, cinematic camera control, and faster inference. Because both sections contain 5+ features, avoid a flat grid; keep one primary visual panel and a supporting list/stack. The two blocks should differ in composition direction and background tone so they do not feel repetitive.

Add a short, credibility-building proof layer using selected testimonial snippets or capability reassurance cards, but keep it secondary to the logo trust bar. This section should bridge the product story into decision confidence without turning into a generic testimonial wall. Use 3 small cards max with a darker surface and bronze accents.

Present the two plan cards in a focused comparison-style treatment, but keep the visual hierarchy clear rather than dense. Seedance 1.5 Pro can carry a stronger price anchor, while Seedream 4.5 should feel quote-led and enterprise-friendly. Emphasize what is included, not a broad pricing matrix. CTAs on both cards must still read 'Get started' to obey the single CTA rule, with accent color at full opacity.

Use a 4-5 item testimonial carousel or compact grid because there are enough quotes to justify it. Keep the layout visually lighter than the pricing section: short quotes, role-first attribution, and one or two emphasized pull quotes from creative directors or video producers. This is the last credibility ramp before conversion, so make it feel human but controlled.

Close with a high-contrast floating lead card that frames the final action as 'see it in action' rather than a generic signup. The section should be compact, premium, and decisive. Keep the CTA button full-width on mobile, accent-filled at 100% opacity, and labeled only 'Get started'. The left side can hold a short conversion reassurance line; the right side can be the form or a minimal request flow.

Do not use a moving marquee. If media/logos are included, keep this as a static footer-adjacent strip with compact partner or press logos. If no strong media logos exist, omit this section in implementation and let the footer close the page cleanly.

blueprint.designPersonality: A premium AI studio for enterprise creators: dark, precise, media-forward, and trust-led. The page should feel like a high-end command center for generating visuals at scale, with logos as the dominant proof signal, warm bronze accents, elevated card surfaces, and a visually rich gallery that makes the model output feel tangible.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a creative media gallery with embedded video tiles, UI mock frames, generation result previews, and floating prompt/parameter chips. Avoid human faces in the hero. Keep the imagery product-centric, cinematic, and interface-led rather than lifestyle-led. Include a dark gallery section with one prominent video tile, two supporting visual tiles, and a capability strip showing image, video, and audio-visual outputs.

designStrategy.reasoning: This page should behave like a high-intent product evaluation landing page for professional buyers. The audience is solution-aware and needs clear proof of capability, especially since the product spans both image and video generation. Because logos are the strongest trust signal, the layout should lead with brand credibility and enterprise readiness rather than heavy storytelling. A split hero is best here: it supports a concise message, a human/professional face element, and a strong CTA without crowding the fold. The page should feel premium, futuristic, and conversion-focused, with balanced section density so technical details remain readable. A creative media gallery is important to demonstrate output quality across both modalities, but it should live below the hero so the top section stays clean and conversion-oriented.
